sentences.text: Heard Smt Shruthi M, learned counsel who represents Sri Vinayakeerthy M, learned counsel who is on record for the appellant as well as Sri D Vijaya Kumar, learned counsel who is appearing for respondent No 2 - Insurance Company.
Issuance of notice to respondent No 1 stood dispensed with.

2. Projecting that the amount awarded as compensation by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Maddur through orders in MVC No. 770/2014 dated 30.03.2015 is inadequate, the claimant is before this Court by way of appeal.

Marking her submission with regard to the merits of the matter, learned counsel for the appellant states that the appellant sustained multiple grievous injuries due to the accident and become permanently disabled.

Learned counsel also submits that though by all evidence the appellant has established before the Tribunal that he become totally and completely disabled and unable to do work, the Tribunal has awarded meager sum as compensation.
Therefore, present appeal is preferred.
Learned counsel thereby seeks enhancement of compensation.

4. Per Contra Sri D Vijaya Kumar, learned counsel for respondent No 2 submits that the Tribunal having considered all the aspects of the case, more particularly the injuries sustained by the appellant has awarded just sum i.e., Rs.11,47,767/- as compensation and therefore the award needs no interference.

Learned counsel also states that there is no evidence to show that appellant is disabled by 100% that too in respect of whole body and therefore the appeal is not maintainable.

sentences.text: 5. A perusal of record goes to show that as against the claim for Rs. 35,60,000/- the Tribunal by subjecting the evidence of PW 1, CW 1, Exs.P4 to P10 and C1 to C3 to scrutiny came to a conclusion that the appellant is entitled to sum of Rs. 11,47,767/- as compensation.
6. It is not in dispute that the appellant sustained sub- throcanteric fracture of right femur, multiple tarsal bone fracture with dislocation of navicular first metatarsal joints.
Also it is not in dispute that appellant underwent surgeries i.e., debridement plus open reduction and internal fixation of medial malleolous and also open reduction of navicular joint.
It is borne by record that the appellant under general anesthesia also underwent left extended sural artery flap, surgical skin graft and flat debridement.
It is also brought on record that removal of K-wire STSG of raw area of left sole with debridement of wound and closure was done under general anesthesia.
By all the evidence produced, the appellant succeeded in establishing that he took treatment as inpatient from 10.06.2012 to 05.09.2012.

The doctor who treated and examined the appellant exhibited his opinion that the appellant has got permanent disability of 45% to right lower limb which is 15% in respect of whole body and also permanent disability of 45% to left ankle and foot which is 15% to the whole body.
The Tribunal having considered the total evidence, came to a conclusion that the disability in respect of the whole body would be not more than 25%.
This Court is not inclined to interfere with the said finding as the said finding is just and appropriate.

8. Coming to the aspect of assessment of income, learned counsel Sri D Vijaya Kumar submits that as the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority takes the notional income of the appellant as Rs.7,000/- p.m. in respect of the accident that occur in the year 2012, the said figure can be taken into consideration.
However, as projected rightly by the learned counsel for the appellant, sufficient material is produced to show that the appellant was agriculturist by the date of accident.
As per version of the appellant, he was owning 30 acres of agricultural land.
Ex.P8 i.e., RTC extract was produced in support of his version.

Therefore, considering occupation of NC: 2024:KHC:21214-DB the appellant as agriculturist by the date of the accident and it is established that the appellant was also in possession of agricultural land by the date of accident, this court considers desirable to take his notional income as Rs.10,000/- p.m.
The multiplier applied i.e., 14 by the Tribunal needs no interference.
Thus the loss of future earnings due to disability come to Rs.4,20,000/- (10000 x 12 x 14 x 25 %).

The increase therefore under this head would be Rs.1,68,000/-.
9.

Coming to the aspect of loss of amenities in life, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/-
under the said head.

However, having considered the evidence produced which reveals that appellant sustained multiple grievous injuries and underwent several surgeries and become disabled by 25%, this Court considers desirable to increase the same by Rs.20,000/-.
10.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.24,000/- towards loss of earnings during laid up period.

Having considered the nature of injuries sustained and the appellant admittedly was in hospital for a long period, this Court is of the view the appellant would NC: 2024:KHC:21214-DB not been in the N S Balaji vs Abdul Razak @ Haris on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62532547/
3 position to attend his normal pursuits at least for a period of six months.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, loss of earnings during the laid up period came to Rs.60,000/- (10000 x 6).

Thus, increase under this head would be Rs.36,000/-.
11.
Thus, enhancement of compensation would be to an extent of Rs.2,24,000/-.

In the light of the forgoing discussion, the following :
ORDER i) The appeal is allowed in part.
ii) The amount awarded as compensation by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal,
Maddur in MVC No. 770/2014 dated 30.03.2015 is enhanced by Rs.2,24,000/-.
iii) The enhanced sum shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
iv) The second respondent is directed to deposit the enhanced sum within a period of six weeks from the date of receipt of copy of this judgment.
NC: 2024:KHC:21214-DB v) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount.
